subject: Lakeview pilot — capacity flightpath & latency commitments

From: Meera Rao <meera@lakeview.ai>

Cc: daniel.cho@lakeview.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing ask + token/latency targets

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our internal product discussion, we want to validate Redwood Dedicated for a 3-month pilot powering two models: a conversational assistant (max context 2k tokens) and a lightweight reranker. Our target SLOs: p95 latency <= 450ms for the assistant at 512-token responses, and p95 <= 120ms for the reranker. Peak traffic looks spiky — we expect short bursts up to ~12k tokens/sec for the assistant for <10 minutes, sustained steady-state of ~1.2k tokens/sec. Reranker calls are synchronous and could be up to 3k calls/sec with ~50 tokens each.

Can you provide a recommended Dedicated pool sizing, expected tokens/sec capacity, latency fit, and recommended safety margin? Also include guidance on burst capacity options and expected costs. Attached is our short requirements deck.

Appreciate it — Meera
Principal Product Manager
Lakeview AI

Attachment: lakeview_requirements_v1.pdf (1 page)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Meera Rao <meera@lakeview.ai>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@lakeview.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask + token/latency targets

Meera — thanks for the clear targets and the deck. High level summary below; detailed numbers and a conservative "flightpath" plan attached.

Quick answer: we can meet the latency SLOs with a Dedicated pool sized to handle ~14k tokens/sec peak for assistant traffic (this includes a 17% safety buffer) and a separate small slab for the reranker to preserve latency. That maps to a baseline of 6 NVIDIA A40-equivalent GPUs for assistant serving and 2 GPUs for the reranker, plus a burst reserve of 2 GPUs (on-demand) to cover the 10-minute spikes.

What I'm attaching: a spreadsheet with token/sec modeling, per-model latency curves by GPU slab, and a diagram of the flightpath (how we phase from pilot to scale). Key assumptions are below; please confirm or correct any workload numbers you have.

Assumptions:
- Assistant: average response length 400 tokens, p95 output 512 tokens; model is a 13B open model (float16) with KV cache enabled.
- Reranker: 50-token invocations, model quantized to int8 when beneficial.
- We budget 40ms of infra overhead for routing + batching; the rest is model execution.
- We assume continuous batching for steady-state; spikes handled by burst pool.

Next steps: If those assumptions hold, we'll produce a final Dedicated proposal and a short ops playbook (runbooks, autoscale policy, fallback variant). Copying Ben and Marissa for capacity validation and cost calibration.

—Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_proposal_v2.xlsx (3 sheets)

Lauren — dug into the numbers from the spreadsheet. Quick notes:
- For the assistant, measured tokens/sec per A40 for similar 13B with our runtime is ~2.0k/sec sustained at p95 <= 400ms when KV cache hits are high and batching latency budget is set to 60ms. That suggests 7 GPUs to reach 14k tokens/sec sustained; my recommendation is to lean to 8 GPUs for steady-state to avoid contention during background maintenance and JVM-level GC spikes in infra services.
- Reranker: we can get ~1.5k calls/sec per GPU at p95 <= 100ms for 50-token runs with int8. Given your 3k calls/sec peak, keep 2 GPUs with autoscale to add 1 GPU on spikes.
- Burst: we model burst capacity as pre-warmed fraction; the 2 GPU burst reserve is good but recommend a warm-start window of 60s to reach full throughput.

I'll attach a capacity sensitivity tab and a simple ops checklist. Marissa, can you validate the SLO math and put rough cost estimates on the sheet?

- Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_flightpath_diagram.png (diagram)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask + token/latency targets

Ben — validated the p95 math and cost roughs. Notes for the proposal:
- Headroom calculation: start with observed tokens/sec requirement (peak 12k) + 17% buffer = 14,040 tokens/sec. Dividing by 1.9k tokens/sec per A40 (conservative baseline) => 7.4 GPUs => round up to 8 for steady-state. Add 2 hot-spare GPUs for burst to give consistent latency during 10-minute peaks.
- KV cache effectiveness: If Lakeview's traffic has high prefix reuse (chat sessions), cache hit rate could reduce GPU compute by ~18% in steady-state. We will instrument early to tune cache TTLs.
- Quantization: If reranker uses int8, we can reduce reranker GPU need to 1.5 GPUs effective — but keep 2 for redundancy.
- Autoscale policy: scale assistant pool by tokens/sec windows (30s TTL) and maintain a minimum headroom of 20% to preserve p95 SLAs during noisy neighbors.

Cost note: estimated pilot run-rate (infra-only) ~ $28k–35k/month depending on reserved vs on-demand pricing. Final quote pending procurement terms.

Marissa
Principal Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask + token/latency targets

Daniel — quick answers inline and attaching an updated sheet that splits cost by pricing shape and lists two fallback variants.

1) Cold-start behavior: burst GPUs pre-warm in 60–90s. Worst-case we observe a p95 latency increase of ~550–700ms during the first 30–60s depending on model warm-up (tokenization + KV population). We can mitigate with a rolling warm pool (keep 1 GPU hot) to reduce the 90s tail to ~350–450ms. We'll include a warm-start runbook in the ops playbook.

2) Costs: Reserved (1yr) pilot pricing estimate: $21k/month infra-only. Month-to-month: $33k/month infra-only. Numbers exclude networking and 3rd-party licensing.

3) Fallbacks: a) Lower-capacity model variant (8-bit quantized 13B) with slightly higher perplexity but 25–30% lower latency; b) Regional fallthrough to hosted clusters with soft-degradation SLAs (p95 shifts up to 800ms). We recommend agreeing on failover order in the contract.

Next steps: If Lakeview is comfortable with the numbers, we'll produce a formal SOW and a canary plan (week 0 smoke, week 1 load ramp, week 2 steady-state). Priya — happy to sync with CloudCap on orchestration details.

Thanks — Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
